setup_steps.detail: Create at api.slack.com/apps; client ID and client secret appear on the App Management page. (doc-stated)

setup_steps.step: Choose minimal bot scopes (scope) and user scopes (user_scope)
setup_steps.detail: Bot and user scope sets must be requested in separate OAuth flows per doc; scopes accumulate across installs, removal requires revoking the token. (doc-stated)

setup_steps.step: Configure HTTPS Redirect URL under OAuth & Permissions
setup_steps.detail: Must be HTTPS, no '#' anchor; redirect_uri must match or be subpath of a configured URL; same value in authorize and access steps if multiple configured, else bad_redirect_uri. (doc-stated)

setup_steps.step: Implement authorize redirect + code exchange at oauth.v2.access
setup_steps.detail: Redirect user to Slack authorize endpoint, receive temporary code at redirect_uri, exchange with client secret for access token. (doc-stated)
Installing needs a user with permission; if the workspace requires approved apps, an Owner/app manager must approve. (doc-stated)

App dashboard > Manage Distribution > complete checklist > Activate Public Distribution. Requires SSL on redirect/request URLs and OAuth 2.0 flow. Yields Add to Slack button and install URL. Not reviewed. (doc-stated)
Submit from app config; automated tests, test accounts with dummy data, demo video; preliminary then functional review. Needs >=10 active workspaces (used within 28 days). (doc-stated)

approval.type: Two layers. (1) Per-workspace admin approval: only if the target workspace has enabled 'Require approved apps'; default is members can install without Owner approval. (2) Slack Marketplace review: optional, but needed to avoid reduced rate limits for new commercially distributed apps. Public distribution itself has no Slack review.
approval.typical_wait: Workspace admin approval: no official number. Marketplace: preliminary feedback up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks new, up to 6 weeks resubmission; cannot be expedited (doc-stated). Public distribution activation: no review, no wait stated.

effort_estimate: Internal/own-workspace app: inferred hours to ~1 day for OAuth code. Public distribution (unlisted): inferred ~days. Marketplace: inferred multi-month (10-business-day preliminary + up to 10 weeks functional + 10-workspace install prerequisite + landing/support/privacy pages, video). No official effort figure exists.

gotchas.text: Since 2025-05-29, commercially distributed apps not in the Marketplace, created on/after that date or newly installed, get Tier 1 on conversations.history and conversations.replies: 1 request/minute, max/default limit param 15. Marketplace apps, existing installs of older unlisted apps, and internal customer-built apps (50+/min, 1000 objects) are unaffected. (doc-stated)
Marketplace requires >=10 active workspaces installed, yet unlisted public distribution is rate-limited; a chicken-and-egg for read-history apps. (inferred from the two doc-stated facts)
Bot and user scopes need separate OAuth flows; Sign in with Slack scopes cannot be combined. (doc-stated)
Scopes accumulate; removing one requires revoking the whole token. (doc-stated)
Once published to Marketplace, distribution cannot be toggled off; must discontinue listing. Deactivating public distribution removes the app from other workspaces. (doc-stated)

Marketplace submission: Slack workspace credentials not accepted as test accounts; apps using only Sign in with Slack or only an MCP server are excluded; use signing secrets not verification tokens; use OAuth state param; TLS 1.2+. (doc-stated)
Published Marketplace app is locked; new scopes/features require resubmission and staging app; installing with unreviewed scopes causes customer errors. (doc-stated)

scopes_notes: Request least privilege; Marketplace requires per-scope justification, no scopes for future features, avoid legacy/restricted scopes, broad history access needs a clear use case, admin scopes generally limited to partner program members (all doc-stated). Specific scope names (e.g. channels:history, chat:write) were not verified in this research.
blockers_and_workarounds: Blocker: workspace requires approved apps -> an Owner or appointed app manager must approve; admins weigh requested permissions, so minimize scopes (doc-stated).

Blocker: Tier 1 history limits for unlisted new apps -> get Marketplace approval, or build as an internal customer-built app per customer workspace (unaffected, doc-stated), or use Events API to receive messages instead of polling (inferred, not stated in sources).
Blocker: Marketplace needs 10 active workspaces -> bootstrap via unlisted public distribution pilots (doc-stated as suited to pilots).
Blocker: creating app / activating distribution / admin approvals are human account actions; an agent cannot do them without the user's logged-in session (inferred).
unverified: Typical wait for workspace admin approval: no official number found.
